_README: Temporal Overlap Pilot -- primary preset (seqsfg/overlap.py).
Two sections, as in the other presets. 'config' is an ordinary seqsfg Config, hashed like any
other, so pilot_config.json, asynchrony_config.json and the rest are untouched. 'overlap' is
this pilot's own section; its parameters are deliberately NOT Config fields, because adding
fields to Config would move the hash of every configuration already run.
QUESTION: does detection of an asynchronous recurring figure depend on the absolute duration
of overlap between its components, on the proportion of them that overlaps, or only on how far
apart their onsets are? Seven cells cross two component durations with several onset steps.
Three comparisons were fixed before any data: equal fraction (20,10) vs (40,20), equal absolute
overlap (20,10) vs (40,30), equal onset separation (20,20) vs (40,20).
WHAT IS HELD FIXED ACROSS ALL SEVEN CELLS, and why it has to be:
background tone duration   40 ms (config tone_dur_ms). Only the FIGURE's components change
length; they carry their own duration (Interval.dur). Changing
tone_dur_ms would change the cloud too.
tone budget                70 per channel, every channel, every cell
frequency pool             24 channels, 200-4865 Hz, one per ERB
level                      one amplitude, 0.026, for background and figure alike
recurrences                8, at a rate drawn from U[420, 500] ms (2.0-2.4 per second)
shared onset jitter        120 ms, the same distribution in every cell
scene duration             4900 ms
The timing is sized for the WIDEST cell: (40, 40) spans 40 + 6*40 = 280 ms, and with 120 ms of
shared jitter one recurrence needs 400 ms, so the inter-recurrence interval starts at 420. That
is slower than the 3 Hz the two-interval pilots used, and it is the same rate in every cell --
the rate is never relaxed for a harder or longer condition. Estimated session about 25 min for
140 main trials.
ABSENT TRIALS hold the same candidate tones as their present counterpart: same channels, same
durations, same amplitude, same count, only the arrangement randomised. The audit checks this
per (frequency, duration) pair, not on the total. Otherwise 'longer tones' would mean 'figure
present' and this would be a duration-detection task in disguise.
KNOWN CONFOUND, not fixed: at equal amplitude a 40 ms component carries about 3 dB more energy
than a 20 ms one. The synchronous cell at each duration is where a general duration benefit
would appear, but it does not remove the confound, and mixture RMS normalisation would not
either -- it equalises the scene, not the component.
The roving control lives in overlap_roving_control.json and answers a different question.
FREQUENCY RANGE AND LEVEL. The pool stops at 4865 Hz rather than the 9486 Hz the earlier
tasks used: a 25-minute session of dense tone clouds with energy near 9 kHz is tiring to
listen to and buys nothing here, since the figure spans 4.6 octaves either way. Holding
the cloud density where the audit was run needed the budget to rise from 58 to 70 tones
per channel, because 24 channels carry fewer simultaneous tones than 30 did.
One tone is calibrated to 60 dB SPL and about 14 sound at once, so the scene sits near 71 dB SPL -- far below
any exposure limit for a session of this length, but calibrate rather than assume.
